speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Minister, you are taking Question Nos 2 and 3 together?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: If I may have your permission to take Question Nos 2 and 3 together?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: First, Mr Seah Kian Peng had asked if HDB will build more BTO flats or advance planned projects in view of demand.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are finalising the details and will announce our plans for 2022 when ready.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Second, there have been concerns over the waiting times for BTO flats, as raised by Miss Cheryl Chan.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Some have said that waiting times have risen to six to seven years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The average waiting time for ongoing BTO projects, including delays brought about by the pandemic, has remained between four and five years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Thus far, Government’s support and assistance measures have helped to keep the pandemic-induced delays to our BTO projects to a year or less, except for one project which had already experienced project difficulties unrelated to the pandemic.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The total wait time for any given project has been kept under six years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For BTO projects launched last year and this year, the estimated waiting times range from three to five and a half years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For example, Hougang Citrine launched in August is expected to be completed in three years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Alkaff Breeze in Bidadari launched in February has a wait time of just over three years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And Garden Court @ Tengah, launched last November, has a waiting time of about three and a half years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There are some projects that will take longer, such as Queen’s Arc – launched in August this year – expected to take longer at about five and a half years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There are a few projects like Queen’s Arc, where the waiting times are longer.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is because the conditions of the site are difficult, and construction will take longer, or these are projects with very high storey-heights, very tall blocks, which require more construction time.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These have caused some people to worry that all new BTOs will take six to seven years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: By and large, barring further unexpected developments, most flat buyers can expect to move into their flats within four to five years after booking their flats.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Third, the recent news on Greatearth’s insolvency may have added to the anxieties of home buyers waiting for their flats to be completed and some are concerned whether this puts the completion of their homes at risk.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: To try to minimise the impact on home buyers, HDB has brought new contractors on board, within a month, to take over Greatearth’s affected projects.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Unfortunately, this will still add a further two to three months' delay to affected projects, but we are working closely with the new contractors to bring the projects back on track.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are watching the progress of all BTO projects closely and have stepped up efforts to detect emerging issues earlier and resolve them.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Fourth, existing home buyers may be concerned about further delays to ongoing projects given the impact of COVID-19 on the construction industry.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: With tightened border controls over foreign workers, disruptions in the supply of building materials and stringent worksite public health measures, there have been manpower and material shortages and a slowdown in work, which have affected public and private construction projects.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: To try to mitigate the pandemic’s impact on our public housing programme, HDB has rolled out extensive assistance to help contractors complete ongoing projects in a timely manner.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: To tackle manpower shortages, HDB has worked with firms to safely recruit workers from various countries and co-shared the increase in manpower costs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: HDB has also worked with contractors to explore ways to speed up construction without affecting safety and quality.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: To minimise work stoppages due to COVID-19 transmission, we have implemented Antigen Rapid Testing, or ART, on top of Rostered Routine Testing (RRT) at worksites.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This allows members of the construction workforce who have been infected to be picked up and treated early, and close contacts quarantined swiftly.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Worksites can then continue operating as long as workers are on the ART regime.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: To help with the higher cost of materials, HDB has extended the period of protection against steel price fluctuation and supplied contractors with more concreting materials at protected prices.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is in addition to the extensive Government support provided through the Job Support Scheme (JSS), construction restart grants, legislative interventions, advance payments, sharing of prolongation costs and manpower cost increases, and foreign worker levy rebates.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: While the pandemic has inevitably caused delays to both private and public sector construction projects, including BTO projects, we will continue to do our best to minimise the extent of the delays.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: HDB has also taken steps to support affected home buyers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have helped some flat buyers secure interim accommodation and will be increasing the supply of flats under the Parenthood Provisional Housing Scheme (PPHS) by 800 units over the next two years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For low-income households with no family support and no other housing options, HDB will consider offering Interim Rental Housing, or IRH on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: With these measures, we will press on to keep our BTO programme on track and support buyers who may be affected by the delays.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: I want to thank the Minister for detailing all the measures that are put in place to ensure the BTO projects will continue in construction, and also to clarify the dates because I have heard a lot of feedback on this aspect.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: The question I want to ask the Minister is, just now he mentioned that progressively there will be more BTOs that will be pushed out, even beyond 17,000 over time.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Given the fact that there is also a very vibrant resale market currently, how is the Ministry going to balance between the resale market, just to make sure that the prices are still healthy, and also the future BTO flats in place?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We continue to keep a close eye on the property market in general, both the private sector as well as the HDB resale market.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There are a range of reasons why demand for housing is high.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: First, of course, this is the Echo Boomer generation, family formation rates, marriage and the desire for housing and their own homes, is one.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Second, the pressures of the pandemic, work from home, changes that we have to adapt and adjust to, have caused people to want more space, in general.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And so, both first-timers as well as even second-timers wanting a bigger place.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Thirdly, interest rates, being as low as they are, have enabled people to be able to consider housing options.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Then, the stresses and strains on the construction sector, the delays in both BTO as well as private housing projects, have caused some people who need homes to consider the resale market, both in the HDB resale as well as the private resale market for private properties.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And the social trends that have been taking place over the years and decades: the desire for more space for more privacy, for more nuclearised families, rather than three-generation families, more singles desiring their own homes and own spaces.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: At the same time, for the resale market, we have provided significant grants to help people afford homes in the resale market, if they need to.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And for those who cannot wait longer for the BTO flats to move to a resale flat because of urgent family needs, we will consider their appeals for waiver of forfeiture for their BTO flats on a case-by-case basis and be sympathetic to their housing needs.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I also welcome the news that there will be more flats that will be built in the coming years; the Minister mentioned more than 17,000.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I am quite sure I am not alone in this House but many of us, each week, we continue to receive many requests and appeals from residents, telling us that they just cannot get their flat early enough; they cannot even have a chance of getting a flat.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I believe that the desired outcomes for all of us must be that we want to give couples their first flat as early as possible.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: So, we need to continue to shorten the waiting time.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Four, five years – can it be shorter?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Because there is really a lot of pent-up demand.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: So, 17,000 now; my first request is, what is the maximum that we could go up to, in order to meet the pent-up demand?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: There are also concerns by residents that whilst waiting for their flat, some of them, their income ceilings may exceed the limits and, therefore, they are disqualified.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: So, my plea to the Minister is that – I do not have the figures obviously, but I am quite sure demand far outstrips supply – let us increase the supply as much as possible to reduce the waiting time and fulfil residents and couples' desire for a flat earlier rather than later.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As I said earlier, we will increase the supply of BTO flats next year, a number larger than the 17,000 we have launched this year.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have been increasing the BTO flats' supply for some years already.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Next year, it will be more than that.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We balance that against the supply in the resale market.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As I said, the demand is high for a whole variety of reasons.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But we have to keep an eye on the overall ecosystem of housing, both public and private, BTOs and resale, to ensure that the overall housing ecosystem remain stable while meeting the aspirations of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: But from my indications, from the appeals that we have received, it seems that rental flats under PPHS are not so forthcoming and there is still some amount of waiting there as well.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: So, can I ask the Minister what is the availability of the rental flats under the PPHS scheme and whether there is enough to meet the demands or requests from new home buyers?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The PPHS provides home buyers with an option if they wish to stay on their own before their flats are ready; these are for married couples especially with children.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The demand for PPHS has grown significantly because of the pandemic arising from the BTO delays as well as the desire for more privacy and, therefore, while waiting for their flats, they want to get PPHS.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, that way we hope to ensure that those with more urgent housing needs while waiting for their BTO flats can get support.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For those with no family support and no housing options, we have other alternatives such as Interim Rental Housing (IRH).

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We continue to see how better we can support families who have been impacted by the delays during this period.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And when people apply for the flats, they book their flats, they get the Housing Loan Eligibility (HLE) as well as their grant eligibility at the point of application.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Therefore, the delays in waiting for flats that they have already booked, there will be less impact on that front.
